## 1 Abstract

Dozens of stability indices are in use, each computed once from the cell
means of a trial. Computed on every posterior draw of the cell means
instead, each index gets a posterior mean, an HPD interval and, for
every genotype, a probability of being the best.
[`bam_indices()`](https://myaseen208.com/bayesammi/reference/bam_indices.md)
does this for five classical indices and
[`bam_ammi_indices()`](https://myaseen208.com/bayesammi/reference/bam_ammi_indices.md)
for six AMMI-based ones. The cell means come from any fit: AMMI or GGE
([`bayes_ammi()`](https://myaseen208.com/bayesammi/reference/bayes_ammi.md))
or a stability model
([`bayes_stability()`](https://myaseen208.com/bayesammi/reference/bayes_stability.md)).

``` r

fit <-
  bayes_ammi(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .nIter  = 3000
    , .k      = 2
    , .burnin = 500
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 2
    , .priors = bam_priors(
          mu_mean     = 0
        , mu_var      = 1e+8
        , tau_mean    = 0
        , tau_var     = 1e+8
        , delta_mean  = 0
        , delta_var   = 1e+8
        , lambda_mean = 0
        , lambda_var  = 1e+8
        , nu          = 1
        , s2          = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .seed   = 11
    , .align  = TRUE
    , .model  = "AMMI"
    , .het    = FALSE
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
```

## 2 Classical indices

For one draw of the cell means \\\eta\_{ij}\\, with interaction
\\\epsilon\_{ij} = \eta\_{ij} - \bar{\eta}\_{i\cdot} -
\bar{\eta}\_{\cdot j} + \bar{\eta}\_{\cdot\cdot}\\:

| Index | Formula | Better |
|----|----|----|
| Wricke’s ecovalence | \\W_i = \sum_j \epsilon\_{ij}^2\\ | smaller |
| Shukla’s stability variance | \\\frac{G}{(G-2)(E-1)}W_i - \frac{\sum_k W_k}{(G-1)(G-2)(E-1)}\\ | smaller |
| Lin and Binns’ superiority | \\\sum_j (\eta\_{ij} - M_j)^2 / (2E)\\, \\M_j\\ the best in environment \\j\\ | smaller |
| Annicchiarico’s reliability | \\\bar{Z}\_i - z\_{1-p} s\_{Z_i}\\, \\Z\_{ij} = 100\\\eta\_{ij}/\bar{\eta}\_{\cdot j}\\ | larger |
| Eskridge’s safety-first | \\\bar{\eta}\_{i\cdot} - z\_{1-\alpha} s_i\\, \\s_i^2\\ the variance across environments | larger |

``` r

ind <-
  bam_indices(
      fit           = fit
    , higher_better = TRUE
    , .prob         = 0.25
    , .alpha        = 0.05
    )
ind
```

    Posterior stability indices (larger values of the trait are better)

    Posterior means; rank_overall is the mean of the expected ranks over the indices (1 = best)

``` r

plot(x = ind)
```

![](data:image/webp;base64,)

The indices measure different things. Wricke’s and Shukla’s indices
measure stability alone and rank genotypes in the same order. Lin and
Binns’ index measures distance from the best, so it mixes mean and
stability. The rank correlation between Wricke’s and Lin and Binns’
posterior means is 0.08. Shukla’s estimator can be negative, as in the
classical analysis; 5 of its 9 HPD intervals reach below zero, a sign
that the stability variance of those genotypes cannot be told from zero.

Because the indices are computed from the cell means, without plot
error, they describe the stability of the expected performance. The HPD
intervals show how well 20 environments determine them; they are wide.

## 3 AMMI-based indices

With coordinates \\\mathrm{PC}\_{ik} = \lambda_k^{1/2}\alpha\_{ik}\\ and
the share \\\theta_k = \lambda_k^2/\sum_m \lambda_m^2\\ of each fitted
term:

| Index | Formula | Source |
|----|----|----|
| ASV | \\\sqrt{(\lambda_1^2/\lambda_2^2\\\mathrm{PC}\_{i1})^2 + \mathrm{PC}\_{i2}^2}\\ | Purchase et al. (2000) |
| SIPC | \\\sum_k \lvert\mathrm{PC}\_{ik}\rvert\\ | Sneller et al. (1997) |
| EV | \\\sum_k \alpha\_{ik}^2 / K\\ | Zobel (1994) |
| Za | \\\sum_k \theta_k \lvert\alpha\_{ik}\rvert\\ | Zali et al. (2012) |
| WAAS | \\\sum_k \theta_k \lvert\mathrm{PC}\_{ik}\rvert\\ | Olivoto et al. (2019) |
| WAASY | mean and WAAS rescaled to 0-100 and weighted | Olivoto et al. (2019) |

``` r

ai <-
  bam_ammi_indices(
      fit           = fit
    , higher_better = TRUE
    , .weight_y     = 50
    )
ai
```

    Posterior AMMI-based stability indices (2 term(s); WAASY with weight 50 on the mean)

``` r

plot(x = ai)
```

![](data:image/webp;base64,)

WAASY gives the mean and the stability equal weights (`.weight_y = 50`).
A breeder who values the mean more raises the weight:

``` r

data.table::rbindlist(
    l = lapply(
        X   = c(30, 50, 70)
      , FUN = function(wy) {
          a <-
            bam_ammi_indices(
                fit           = fit
              , higher_better = TRUE
              , .weight_y     = wy
              )
          a$indices[index == "WAASY"][order(-mean)][1:3, list(weight = wy, Gen, mean, prob_best)]
        }
      )
  )
```

## 4 Indices from a stability model

The same classical indices can be computed from the cell means of a
[`bayes_stability()`](https://myaseen208.com/bayesammi/reference/bayes_stability.md)
fit:

``` r

fs <-
  bayes_stability(
      .data   = Maiz
    , .y      = y
    , .gen    = entry
    , .env    = site
    , .rep    = rep
    , .model  = "ER"
    , .nIter  = 2000
    , .burnin = 500
    , .thin   = 1
    , .chains = 1
    , .priors = bam_stab_priors(
          mu_var = NULL
        , g_var  = NULL
        , h_var  = NULL
        , b_var  = 100
        , nu     = 1
        , s2     = NULL
        , nu_d   = 1
        , s2_d   = NULL
        )
    , .level  = 0.95
    , .alpha  = 0.05
    , .seed   = 11
    , .waic   = TRUE
    )
bam_indices(
    fit           = fs
  , higher_better = TRUE
  , .prob         = 0.25
  , .alpha        = 0.05
  )$means
```

## 5 Interpretation

``` r

bam_interpret(
    x             = ind
  , higher_better = TRUE
  , top           = 5
  )
```

    Posterior stability indices

    Best on average over the indices (mean expected rank): 6, 5, 3, 7 and 2.

    Findings:
    - Most probably the best on wricke: 7 (probability 0.45).
    - Most probably the best on shukla: 7 (probability 0.45).
    - Most probably the best on lin_binns: 6 (probability 0.71).
    - Most probably the best on annicchiarico: 6 (probability 0.71).
    - Most probably the best on safety_first: 6 (probability 0.54).
    - The indices disagree on the best genotype: they weigh mean and stability
      differently.

    Recommendations:
    - Prefer genotypes that rank well on several indices and whose HPD intervals
      separate from the others; overlapping intervals mean the trial cannot tell
      them apart.

    Cautions:
    - Stability indices describe the environments of this trial; confirm over
      years before recommending.

    Sources:
    - Wricke, G. (1962). Uber eine Methode zur Erfassung der okologischen
      Streubreite in Feldversuchen. Zeitschrift fur Pflanzenzuchtung, 47, 92-96.
    - Shukla, G. K. (1972). Some statistical aspects of partitioning
      genotype-environmental components of variability. Heredity, 29(2), 237-245.
      doi:10.1038/hdy.1972.87
    - Lin, C. S. and Binns, M. R. (1988). A superiority measure of cultivar
      performance for cultivar x location data. Canadian Journal of Plant
      Science, 68(1), 193-198. doi:10.4141/cjps88-018
    - Annicchiarico, P. (1992). Cultivar adaptation and recommendation from
      alfalfa trials in Northern Italy. Journal of Genetics and Breeding, 46,
      269-278.
    - Eskridge, K. M. (1990). Selection of stable cultivars using a safety-first
      rule. Crop Science, 30, 369-374.
